licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets map cleanly onto the dominant clusters in the data: deceptive license procurement, fraud/misrepresentation during practice, criminal convictions, competence/negligence failures, broad unprofessional/ethics violations, substance or health impairment, statutory or regulatory non-compliance, reciprocal out-of-state discipline, and facilitating unlicensed practice—together covering virtually every item with minimal overlap and no large residual.

profession_specific.license_type_structu.rationale: The data clusters naturally by credential type (licensed vs. certified), scope title (dietitian-only, nutritionist-only, or combined dietitian-nutritionist), technician-level credentials, and limited-duration permits (provisional, temporary, graduate), with a small catch-all for outliers like compact privileges and title-protection designations.

profession_specific.alternative_credenti.rationale: The items cluster into five natural groups: the Certified Nutrition Specialist (CNS/BCNS) credential, the American Clinical Board of Nutrition Diplomate (DACBN), the American Board of Nutrition (ABN) diplomate/membership, professional society memberships (AIN, ASCN), and the one academic-degree-based pathway (CA master's degree route).

profession_specific.protected_titles.rationale: The titles cluster naturally by the core role word(s) they contain—dietitian-only, nutritionist-only, hybrid dietitian/nutritionist, nutrition therapy practitioner variants, and dietetic technician—while a separate bucket captures the many credential abbreviations (LD, RD, LDN, C.D., etc.) that appear alongside the spelled-out titles.
